quality.usable: An accurate, helpful target that satisfies the request; minor non-material wording flaws may remain.
quality.incorrect: A serious factual, unsupported-content, language, format, or instruction-following error is identifiable.
quality.ambiguous: Missing context or unresolved interpretations prevent a unique or well-scoped target judgment.
quality.unclear: Verification was insufficient for a confident judgment.

safety.benign: No harmful assistance or materially hazardous recommendation identified in the request/reference pair.
safety.unsafe: Materially hazardous advice or information identified, including misleading emergency assessment.
safety.unclear: Available evidence is insufficient to resolve safety.

method: Read all selected request/reference pairs and their exact source IDs.
Used supplied context for passage-grounded extraction and general knowledge for straightforward language and factual tasks.
Conducted limited external reference checks through gstack browse in an isolated browser state.
Made no corrected targets, dataset edits, filtering operations, or training runs.

principal_observations.issue: Unanswered requests, contradictory explanations, corrupt names, and mistranslated technical terminology
Unidentified subjects and ambiguous passage continuations
Repeated or closely related prompts with differing targets

limitations: These are provisional automated judgments from one reviewer, not independent human or native-speaker validation.
Only the 100 Korean training records were in scope. No development, calibration, confirmation, model-output, review-pack, score, or existing evaluation-annotation material was inspected.
External verification was limited, not exhaustive. Several requested pages were unavailable and a search attempt was blocked; unresolved claims were retained as unclear.
The source lacks dates or identifying context for some current-policy, career, health, and historical questions; apparent plausibility was not treated as verification of detailed niche claims.
Safety labels concern the supplied pair and do not establish clinical correctness for every benign item.
Counts describe this fixed training subset only. No model improvement, held-out performance, or benefit from filtering has been measured or claimed.
